data.requirement: Links should expire after N days.

data.summary: Turned "links should expire after N days" into a scoped requirement with testable acceptance criteria, recorded assumptions and open questions.

data.text: N is a single global, configurable value in this iteration, not set per link
data.rationale: The requirement names one "N" and does not mention per-link control. Per-link expiry adds API surface and is listed as a question.

data.text: Expiry is measured from the link's creation timestamp
data.rationale: "Expire after N days" most plainly means age since creation. Sliding expiry based on last access is a different feature.

data.text: Expired links stop resolving but are not physically deleted as part of this requirement
data.rationale: Deletion and code reuse are irreversible and were not requested. Keeping the record is the safer default.

data.text: N is set through Spring configuration, e.g. `shortener.link.expiry-days`, and applies to all links.
The default N is 30 days. This is a placeholder until a human confirms it.
A link expires at exactly `createdAt + N × 24h`, computed in UTC from an injectable `java.time.Clock` so tests can control time. Calendar-day and timezone semantics are not used.
Resolving an expired link returns HTTP 410 Gone with no redirect. A link that never existed keeps its current response, presumably 404.
Expiry is computed at resolve time from `createdAt` and the current N. Changing N therefore affects existing links too.
Existing links that are already older than N days become expired as soon as the feature is deployed.
The short code of an expired link is not reissued to a new link.
Link creation and lookup API responses expose an `expiresAt` field. This is a minor additive change.
What should N be by default, and must it be per-environment configurable only, or should API callers be able to set a per-link expiry?
Should expiry count from creation (fixed) or from last access (sliding)?
Should expiry apply retroactively to existing links? This could break many live links at deploy time, which is high impact. Should there be a grace period or migration instead?
What should an expired link return: 410 Gone, 404 Not Found, or a redirect to an "expired" page?
Should expired links eventually be purged from storage, and may their short codes be reused?
Should some links be able to never expire (e.g., N = 0 or a per-link flag)?
Is "days" meant as 24-hour periods (assumed) or calendar days in some timezone?

data.detail: Turned "links should expire after N days" into a scoped requirement with testable acceptance criteria, recorded assumptions and open questions.
7 question(s) left open; assumptions accepted by auto (--auto-approve)

data.summary: Broke the link-expiry requirement into 16 dependency-ordered tasks across design, implement, tests, docs, validate and release, and marked which can run in parallel.

data.text: Start with a discovery task (T1) before any implementation.
data.rationale: The analysis does not say whether `createdAt` is stored, whether redirect caching exists, or what unknown codes currently return. All three decide whether T8, T9 and parts of T12 are needed.

data.text: Make the migration (T8) and cache fix (T9) conditional tasks.
data.rationale: They are only needed if T1 finds that `createdAt` is missing or that redirects are cached. Planning them as conditional avoids inventing work.

data.text: Put a human approval gate (T16) before release.
data.rationale: Retroactive expiry (criterion 7) and any `createdAt` backfill can break live links at deploy time. The requirement analysis flags both as high impact.

data.text: Use a typed, validated configuration-properties class for `shortener.link.expiry-days`.
data.rationale: Spring Boot's binding and validation fail startup with a message naming the property, which meets criterion 2 without custom code.

data.text: Define "expired" as `now >= createdAt + N days`.
data.rationale: Criteria 3 and 4 put the boundary exactly at T + N days.

data.text: `expiresAt` is computed from `createdAt` and N each time, never stored. This follows from criterion 9: changing N and restarting changes expiry for all links.
Short codes are never reused today, because generation checks for existing codes and nothing deletes them. Criterion 8 therefore needs only test coverage, not new logic. T1 confirms this.
The expiry check runs in the service layer, not in a scheduled job. Purge jobs are out of scope.
Has a human approved retroactive expiry of links created before this feature (criterion 7)? Or should existing links get a grace period?
If `createdAt` is missing for existing rows, what backfill value is approved? Options include migration time or a known historical date.
What status do unknown codes return today (for example 404)? Tests in T12 need this to pin the "unchanged" behaviour.

data.detail: Broke the link-expiry requirement into 16 dependency-ordered tasks across design, implement, tests, docs, validate and release, and marked which can run in parallel.

data.summary: Impact analysis for global N-day link expiry. No schema change is needed because `created_at` already exists and is NOT NULL. The changes are the config properties, `UrlService.resolve`, the exception handler, two response DTOs, the controller's OpenAPI docs and the tests.

data.text: Compute `expiresAt` on the fly as `createdAt + N days` and do not persist an `expires_at` column
data.rationale: Criterion 9 requires a config change plus restart to re-expire all links, existing and new. A stored value would go stale, and `created_at` already exists for every row.

data.text: Put the expiry logic in one place, a new `LinkExpiryPolicy` component (or equivalent methods on `UrlService`), used by both the service and the controller
data.rationale: `/shorten`, `/{code}` and `/stats/{code}` all need the same calculation. Duplicating it risks off-by-one differences at the boundary (`>=` versus `>`).

data.text: Treat `GET /stats/{code}` as the "link lookup" endpoint. It gains `expiresAt` but keeps returning 200 for expired links
data.rationale: The requirement only applies expiry to resolution (the redirect). Lookup only has to expose `expiresAt`.

data.text: Treat "N days" as `Duration.ofDays(N)`, that is N × 24h on UTC instants
data.rationale: Criterion 4's example of T + 7d is instant arithmetic. The app clock is UTC, so daylight-saving changes do not apply.

data.text: A redirect to an expired link does NOT increment `click_count` or update `last_accessed_at`. The requirement says no redirect happens, so no click is counted.
The expiry check and any click recording use a single `clock.instant()` value captured once per request.
The 410 body is an RFC 9457 problem detail, matching the existing error style.
The 404 body for unknown codes stays exactly as it is today.
Other agents add no new dependency (for example `spring-boot-starter-validation`) unless they choose it. Validating in the record's compact constructor works without one.

Which datasource does production use? The only config shown is in-memory H2 (`jdbc:h2:mem`), so no rows survive a restart and criterion 7 has no real effect at deploy. If production uses a persistent database, how many live links are older than 30 days and would start returning 410 on deploy? This needs human approval.
Should `/stats/{code}` for an expired link keep returning 200 (assumed here), or should it also signal expiry, for example with an `expired: true` flag or a 410?
Should a request to an expired link be counted anywhere, such as a separate counter or a log/metric? It is currently assumed to be not counted.
Should the 410 response carry `Cache-Control: no-store`? Under RFC 9111, 410 is cacheable by default. A cached 410 could outlive an increase of N (criterion 9 revives links).

data.detail: Impact analysis for global N-day link expiry. No schema change is needed because `created_at` already exists and is NOT NULL. The changes are the config properties, `UrlService.resolve`, the exception handler, two response DTOs, the controller's OpenAPI docs and the tests.

data.summary: Technical design for global N-day link expiry. It covers the exact config property, the new `LinkExpiryPolicy` and `LinkExpiredException`, the changed constructor and method signatures, the 410 contract, the `expiresAt` field on two DTOs, no schema change, and a test and docs split that the implement, tests and docs agents can follow in parallel.

data.text: No schema change, migration or backfill. Expiry is computed as `createdAt + N days`, never stored.
data.rationale: `url_mapping.created_at` already exists and is NOT NULL for every row. Computing expiry at read time also makes AC9 (changing N and restarting re-evaluates all links) automatic.

data.text: Add a nested record `ShortenerProperties.Link(int expiryDays)` as a third component `link` of `ShortenerProperties`. Put `@DefaultValue` on the `link` component and `@DefaultValue("30")` on `expiryDays`. A compact constructor throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the value is below 1.
data.rationale: This meets AC1 and AC2 without adding a dependency. A non-numeric value already fails binding with a `BindException` that names `shortener.link.expiry-days`. Existing accessors stay source-compatible.

data.text: "N days" means `Duration.ofDays(N)` (N × 24h) added to the UTC `Instant`. A link is expired when `!now.isBefore(expiresAt)`, which is the same as `now >= expiresAt`.
data.rationale: This matches AC3 and AC4 exactly (T+7d−1s is active, T+7d is expired). Instants have no DST or calendar ambiguity.

data.text: New `@Component` `LinkExpiryPolicy(ShortenerProperties)` with `Instant expiresAt(UrlMapping)` and `boolean isExpired(UrlMapping, Instant now)`. It holds no `Clock`.
data.rationale: It is the single source of truth for the rule. `now` always comes from the injected `Clock` in `UrlService`, which satisfies AC10 and keeps the policy a pure, trivially unit-testable function.

data.text: `UrlService.resolve` reads `now` once, looks up the link (404 if missing), then throws `LinkExpiredException` before `recordClick` if the link is expired.
data.rationale: AC5 keeps unknown codes at 404, distinct from 410. Expired links must not count clicks. Throwing before the controller calls `.location(...)` guarantees there is no `Location` header (AC4).

data.text: `LinkExpiredException` maps to `ProblemDetail` with status 410 in `ApiExceptionHandler`.
data.rationale: This is consistent with the existing RFC 9457 error bodies.

data.text: Append `Instant expiresAt` as the last component of `ShortenResponse` and `StatsResponse`. The controller fills it from `LinkExpiryPolicy`.
data.rationale: AC6 requires an additive field with existing fields unchanged. Appending keeps the existing JSON order.

data.text: `UrlService.shorten` truncates `clock.instant()` to `ChronoUnit.MICROS` before saving.
data.rationale: The column is `TIMESTAMP(6)`. Truncating makes `expiresAt` from `POST /shorten` (built from the in-memory entity) equal `expiresAt` from `GET /stats` (read from the DB). Existing tests use whole-second clocks and are unaffected.

data.text: `GET /stats/{code}` keeps returning 200 for expired links, with their `expiresAt`.
data.rationale: The requirement only changes resolution. AC8 keeps expired links stored, and stats is the "link lookup" response in AC6.

data.text: No cache headers are added to the 410 response in this change.
data.rationale: The requirement does not ask for them. This is raised as a QUESTION because a cached 410 could outlive a later increase of N.

data.text: The "link lookup response" in AC6 is `GET /stats/{code}` (`StatsResponse`). There is no other lookup endpoint.

Spring Boot 4 / Jackson 3 serialises `Instant` as an ISO-8601 string ending in `Z` (Jackson 3 defaults `WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS` to false). Tests must assert the format explicitly. If this assumption fails, the implement agent must configure it, not change the contract.
"Names the property" in AC2 is satisfied if the startup failure's exception chain or stack trace contains `shortener.link.expiry-days`. It is not required to be in the top-level message.
Expired links are not counted as clicks, and resolving them does not update `lastAccessedAt`.
The 410 body is the default `ProblemDetail` rendered as `application/problem+json`, with no extra fields such as `expiresAt`.

Do you approve retroactive expiry (AC7)? With the default N=30, every link older than 30 days returns 410 immediately on deploy. What datasource does production use? The configured H2 is in-memory, so the real exposure depends on that.
Should the 410 response send `Cache-Control: no-store`? Without it, raising N later (AC9) may not revive links for clients or proxies that cached the heuristically cacheable 410.
Should `GET /stats/{code}` behave differently for expired links, for example by adding an `expired` boolean, instead of returning a normal 200?

data.detail: Technical design for global N-day link expiry. It covers the exact config property, the new `LinkExpiryPolicy` and `LinkExpiredException`, the changed constructor and method signatures, the 410 contract, the `expiresAt` field on two DTOs, no schema change, and a test and docs split that the implement, tests and docs agents can follow in parallel.

data.summary: Created `docs/features/link-expiry.md`, the user-facing guide to global N-day link expiry. It covers behaviour, API changes with curl examples, error cases, the `shortener.link.expiry-days` setting and upgrade notes.

data.text: Put all the content the design asked for in the README section and CHANGELOG entry into one file, `docs/features/link-expiry.md`.
data.rationale: I may only write under `docs/`, and the task asks for one Markdown file under `docs/features/`. `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` sit outside that path.

data.text: Left out bodies for 404, 400 and 429 responses and said only that they are unchanged.
data.rationale: Neither the design nor the requirements give those bodies, and writing them out would invent a contract.

data.text: Described the expiry window as exactly N×24 hours in UTC, not N calendar days.
data.rationale: The design uses `Duration.ofDays(N)` on an `Instant`, and the acceptance criteria say `createdAt` plus N×24h.

data.text: Marked the retroactive expiry of existing links as "pending human approval" in the upgrade notes.
data.rationale: Both upstream stages flag it as a release gate. The doc should not read as if it were already approved.

data.text: Examples use the base URL `http://localhost:8080`, matching the `shortUrl` example in the design.
Existing rows already have a usable `createdAt`, because the design says no schema change or backfill is needed.
The default UTC timestamp format (no fractional seconds when they are zero) applies to `createdAt` and `lastAccessedAt` as well as `expiresAt`. The doc only states the format rule for `expiresAt`.
Should someone with access outside `docs/` add the README section and CHANGELOG entry the design asks for, perhaps by linking to this file? Or is this feature doc enough?
Has the retroactive expiry been approved? If so, should the doc give a specific value of N or an approved migration approach (for example, temporarily raising N) for the first deploy?

Is any redirect caching in place, such as a CDN, a reverse proxy or `Cache-Control` on the 302? The requirements say caches must not serve a link past `expiresAt`, but the design does not cover this, so the doc does not mention it.

data.detail: Created `docs/features/link-expiry.md`, the user-facing guide to global N-day link expiry. It covers behaviour, API changes with curl examples, error cases, the `shortener.link.expiry-days` setting and upgrade notes.

data.summary: Implemented global N-day link expiry as designed: the `shortener.link.expiry-days` property (default 30, minimum 1), `LinkExpiryPolicy`, `LinkExpiredException` mapped to 410, `expiresAt` on `/shorten` and `/stats`, and the OpenAPI and properties docs.

data.text: Changed the `UrlService` constructor to the design's exact 5-argument signature and did not keep the old 4-argument one
data.rationale: The design fixes the constructor and the tests agent is updating `UrlServiceTest` to match. A second constructor would need `@Autowired` to pick one and an extra default `LinkExpiryPolicy`, which the design does not ask for.

data.text: `resolve` reads `clock.instant()` once, before the lookup, and uses that value for both the expiry check and `recordClick`
data.rationale: The design lists this step order, and one instant keeps the expiry decision and the recorded access time consistent.

data.text: The 410 body uses `ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail`, the same as the existing 404 handler
data.rationale: Spring MVC fills `instance` with the request path and sets `application/problem+json`, which matches the contract `{"type":"about:blank","title":"Gone","status":410,...,"instance":"/<code>"}`.

data.text: Added no `Cache-Control` headers
data.rationale: The 302 response has never sent cache headers and the design leaves `redirect` unchanged, so nothing can cache a redirect past `expiresAt`.

data.text: No production code calls the old two-argument `ShortenerProperties(baseUrl, rateLimit)` constructor; I checked only `src/main`. Tests that build the record directly must pass a `Link`, as the design's `LinkExpiryPolicyTest` already does.

Boot 4 with Jackson 3 serialises `Instant` as ISO-8601 with a `Z` suffix and trims trailing zero fractions. This is already the case for `createdAt` today. `shorten` truncates to microseconds, so at most 6 fractional digits appear.

Retroactive expiry (AC7) will break every existing link older than 30 days as soon as this is deployed. Does a human approve this behaviour and the default N=30 for release, or should the first rollout use a larger N?
Should the old 4-argument `UrlService` constructor stay as a deprecated overload for any callers outside this repository? I assumed there are none.

data.detail: Implemented global N-day link expiry as designed: the `shortener.link.expiry-days` property (default 30, minimum 1), `LinkExpiryPolicy`, `LinkExpiredException` mapped to 410, `expiresAt` on `/shorten` and `/stats`, and the OpenAPI and properties docs.

data.summary: Added expiry tests covering the policy, service, properties binding, a fixed-clock integration test for AC3–AC8 and an API-contract integration test; changed only the constructor call in `UrlServiceTest` so it compiles.

data.text: `UrlServiceTest` changes only the `UrlService` constructor call. The new service tests go in `UrlServiceExpiryTest`.
data.rationale: The design changes the constructor, so the old file would not compile. The brief says to add new classes rather than rewrite existing ones.

data.text: The design's `ShortenerIntegrationTest` assertions (`expiresAt` format and the 410 entry in `/v3/api-docs`) are in a new `LinkExpiryApiContractIntegrationTest` instead.
data.rationale: The brief says to add new classes. The new class uses the same `@SpringBootTest` properties, so the cached context is reused.

data.text: AC8 "codes never reassigned" is tested end to end with `@MockitoSpyBean CodeGenerator`. The spy is forced to return the code of an expired link first.
data.rationale: This proves that a code which still exists in storage after expiry is skipped by the real collision check, not just by a mock.

data.text: The 410 test asserts `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance` and the `application/problem+json` content type.
data.rationale: The design's API table lists all of these fields as the contract.

data.text: Jackson writes `Instant` values as ISO-8601 strings that match `Instant.toString()` (no fractional seconds when they are zero), as the design's `expiresAt` rules state.
Spring fills in `ProblemDetail.instance` with the request path when the handler leaves it null.
The H2 database `jdbc:h2:mem:shortener` is shared across contexts and test methods in one JVM. Each seeded code is therefore used exactly once: `exp0001` to `exp0006` and `fresh06`.
AC2's "fails to start" is checked at the binding level with `ApplicationContextRunner`, as the design specifies. No full application boot is attempted.
Should a human approve retroactive expiry (AC7) before release? The tests assert it, but the release gate in the design is still open.
AC9 (restart with a new N) is checked only at the policy level, by comparing N=7 and N=30 on the same mapping. Is that enough, or is a restart-style test with two contexts wanted?

data.detail: Added expiry tests covering the policy, service, properties binding, a fixed-clock integration test for AC3–AC8 and an API-contract integration test; changed only the constructor call in `UrlServiceTest` so it compiles.
